## Exercise 1: Tumour growth over time

This exercise follows the
[tidy data chapter](https://ds4biomed.tech/clean-data-tidy.html)
of *Data Science for the Biomedical Sciences*.
Mice with a human glioma xenograft were assigned to one of 4 groups:
control (`1.CTR`), drug (`2.D`), radiation (`3.R`),
or drug and radiation (`4.D+R`).
Tumour size (mm³) was measured over 28 days.

`data/tumorgrowth_wide.csv` is ds4biomed's
`data/tumorgrowth_long.csv`
([`chendaniely/ds4biomed`](https://github.com/chendaniely/ds4biomed/tree/learner/data),
`learner` branch),
renamed because it's in wide format:
a version of the `tumorgrowth` data
from the [`medicaldata`](https://github.com/higgi13425/medicaldata) GitHub repository.

```{r}
tumor <- read_csv("data/tumorgrowth_wide.csv")
tumor
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Which tidy-data problem does this table have?
2. Pivot the day columns into `day` and `size`,
   with `day` as an integer, dropping missing sizes.
   Call the result `tumor_tidy`.
3. Calculate the mean tumour size for each group on each day.
4. Plot each mouse's tumour size over time, coloured by group.

```{r}
#| eval: false
tumor_tidy <- tumor |>
  pivot_longer(
    `0`:last_col(),
    names_to = ____,
    names_transform = list(day = as.integer),
    values_to = ____,
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  )

tumor_tidy |>
  group_by(____, ____) |>
  summarize(avg_size = mean(size))

ggplot(tumor_tidy, aes(x = day, y = size, group = ID, colour = ____)) +
  geom_line()
```
:::

## Exercise 2: Cleaning a clinical trial dataset

`opt` is the Obstetrics and Periodontal Therapy trial
from the lab's gum health exercise.
This time we'll get it ready to model birth weight.
It has 171 columns, so start with the ones you need.

```{r}
opt |>
  select(PID, Group, Age, BMI, Birth.outcome, Birthweight) |>
  glimpse()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Count the values of `Birth.outcome`.
   What's odd about the labels?
2. How many rows does `filter(opt, Birth.outcome == "Live birth")` return?
   Why?
3. Make `opt_clean`:
   trim the spaces from `Birth.outcome` with `str_trim()`,
   keep live births only,
   relabel `Group` as `control` and `treatment`,
   and keep `PID`, `Clinic`, `Group`, `Age`, `BMI`,
   `Birthweight` and `GA.at.outcome`.
4. How many values are missing in each column of `opt_clean`?

```{r}
#| eval: false
opt_clean <- opt |>
  mutate(
    Birth.outcome = ____,
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("C", "T"),
                   labels = c(____, ____))
  ) |>
  filter(____) |>
  select(____)

opt_clean |>
  summarize(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x))))
```
:::

This is the `opt_clean` that [Linear regression](04-linear-regression.qmd) starts from.

## Exercise 3: Cytomegalovirus

`cytomegalovirus` (from `medicaldata`) follows 64 patients
after a stem cell transplant
([Sobecks et al., 2011](https://higgi13425.github.io/medicaldata/reference/cytomegalovirus.html)).
`cmv` is whether CMV reactivated (0 = no, 1 = yes),
and `recipient.cmv` and `donor.cmv` are the CMV serostatus
of the patient and the donor (0 = negative, 1 = positive).

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Make `cmv`: recode `cmv` as a factor with labels `no` and `yes`,
   and `recipient.cmv` and `donor.cmv` as factors
   with labels `negative` and `positive`.
2. How many values are missing in `time.to.transplant`?

```{r}
#| eval: false
cmv <- cytomegalovirus |>
  mutate(
    cmv = factor(____, levels = ____, labels = ____),
    recipient.cmv = ____,
    donor.cmv = ____
  )
```
:::

You'll model `cmv` in
[Extra practice: logistic regression](09-practice-logistic-regression.qmd).
